parsed.explanation: The write-up's entire finiteness input is the 'finite blocker' fact: a pairwise intersecting family of finite sets has finitely many inclusion-minimal finite transversals. This is false. Take F_k = {x_1,...,x_k, y_k} for k >= 1: any two members share x_1, yet {x_k, y_1,...,y_{k-1}} is a minimal finite transversal for every k, so there are infinitely many. Hence the Koenig/pruning argument (whose 'retain' and 'contract' rules are indeed undefined) cannot be repaired. The write-up uses no arithmetic input at all -- no bound like a_1^2 on relevant primes, no large-prime erasure -- so L6.2 is nowhere established; it needs a genuinely new number-theoretic lemma.
